Class Cp210xSerial

java.lang.Object
io.github.jabrena.juno.hardware.device.usb.Cp210xSerial
public final class Cp210xSerial extends Object
A Silicon Labs CP210x USB-to-UART bridge (CP2102, CP2104, ...) attached to a UsbHostShield: the chip on the RoboPeak RPLIDAR adapter and on many ESP32 and sensor boards. It opens the bridge at 8N1 and a chosen baud rate, moves bytes over the bridge's bulk endpoints, and drives its DTR and RTS lines. 
UsbHostShield usb = new UsbHostShield();
Cp210xSerial serial = new Cp210xSerial(usb);       // once, at startup
if (usb.begin() && serial.begin(115_200)) {
    int value = serial.read();                      // -1 when nothing arrived
}

Allocation: the constructor allocates a 64-byte configuration buffer, a 64-byte receive buffer and a 4-byte request buffer; reading and writing are allocation-free. Nothing arrives unless the program calls read() (or available()) often enough: the bridge only buffers about 576 bytes, half a second at 115200 baud.

  • Method Details

    • begin

      public boolean begin(int baudRate)
      Enumerates the device on the shield, checks it is a CP210x, selects its configuration, and opens its UART at baudRate, 8N1, with DTR and RTS low. Returns false when no device is connected, it is not a CP210x, it has no bulk endpoints, or it refuses a request; lastError() then holds the failing code.

    • isOpen

      public boolean isOpen()
      Whether begin(int) opened the bridge and no transfer has failed since: a failed bulk transfer (the device unplugged, or it stopped answering) closes it, and begin(int) opens it again.

    • lastError

      public int lastError()
      The last negative UsbHostShield code a call failed with, or 0.

    • setBaudRate

      public boolean setBaudRate(int baudRate)
      Changes the UART's baud rate. Returns false when the bridge refuses it.

    • setDtr

      public boolean setDtr(boolean asserted)
      Drives the DTR line: true is the asserted (active, electrically low) state.

    • setRts

      public boolean setRts(boolean asserted)
      Drives the RTS line: true is the asserted (active, electrically low) state.

    • flush

      public void flush()
      Drops every byte the bridge and this driver hold, in both directions.

    • available

      public int available()
      The bytes ready to read() without asking the bridge again: when none are buffered, polls the bridge for one packet first. Returns 0 when nothing arrived, or a negative code when the device stopped answering (which closes the bridge).

    • read

      public int read()
      The next received byte, 0..255, or -1 when nothing arrived (or the device stopped answering).

    • read

      public int read(byte[] buffer, int offset, int length)
      Copies up to length received bytes into buffer[offset], polling the bridge at most once. Returns the bytes copied (0 when nothing arrived), or a negative code when the device stopped answering.

    • write

      public boolean write(int value)
      Sends one byte. Returns false when the device refused it.

    • write

      public boolean write(byte[] data, int offset, int length)
      Sends length bytes from data[offset]. Returns false when the device refused them.
